messages:
Alex: Heads-up — enabling FP8 warmstart on L40S canary triggered kernel-election oscillation + KV cache churn. Seeing frequent back-and-forth between INT8 and FP8 kernels and a bunch of latency spikes. p50 jumped from ~12ms to 45ms during the window.

Alex: snippet from canary logs:
```
[2026-03-15T14:12:01Z] kernel_choice: INT8_fast -> FP8_fallback -> INT8_fast -> FP8_linear (x6 within 2s)
[2026-03-15T14:12:01Z] kv_cache_misses: 42 -> 860 in 3s
[2026-03-15T14:12:02Z] batch_size: 1 -> 4 -> 1 (microbatching spikes)
```

Priya: ugh, that pattern smells like selector threshold hysteresis + kv warmup too short. Can you attach the profiler trace and the kernel-selector dump? need TRACE_ID + selector-state at the time.

Alex: upload: https://redwood.dev/traces/2355506789/canary-warmstart (perf + selector dump)

Ben: quick profiler excerpt I pulled:
```
$ rprof dump --range 14:11:58-14:12:05 --svc=runtime-proxy
kernel_selector: hotpath_switches=7, avg_choice_latency=3.6ms
queue_depth: mean=1.3, max=9
kv_metrics: global_miss_rate=0.18 -> spike 0.72
GPU occupancy: 42% -> 18% during flaps
```

Sara: looks like TransformerEngine auto-mux is flipping between FP8_linear and FP8_fallback kernels when sequence length / occupancy crosses thresholds. On L40S we saw this before when TE's mux has conservative fallbacks. Try pinning TE mux to a single FP8 kernel for the canary to see if it stabilizes.

Mike: also interesting — microbatching is increasing transient batch_size which makes selector see different perf profiles. Two quick experiments: bump kv.warmup_window_ms from 50 -> 200 and disable microbatch merge for the canary route. If that reduces selector flips, we can re-enable gradual batching. I'll schedule AB tomorrow.

Priya: another angle — calibration drift: our fp8 calibrator may under-estimate activation ranges for long contexts and TE is switching to safer fallback kernels. Did we run the new per-layer calibration on the full canary dataset?

Alex: we used the quick calibrator (1000 steps) not full per-layer. Good call — I'll re-run with per-layer baseline and attach results.

Ben: I parsed the selector dump — found threshold hysteresis at 0.12 +/- 0.01 where multiple requests flip it repeatedly. Proposal: increase hysteresis margin and add a 200ms hold-time after kernel switch to avoid thrash.

Sara: Agree. If we add hold-time + pin TE mux on FP8_linear and bump kv warmup, should be fairly deterministic. If latency is still bad, revert FP8 warmstart and fallback to INT8 until calibrator is improved.

infra-bot: Deploy event: canary-l40s v2.3.1 rolled at 2026-03-15T14:10:00 by ci/deploy-bot (link: https://ci.redwood.dev/builds/9876) :deploy:

Alex: Plan of action: 1) run per-layer calibrator (Alex) 2) bump kv.warmup & add selector hold-time (Ben) 3) pin TE mux for canary and disable microbatch merge (Mike/Sara) 4) run AB for 12h and compare p50/p95 + kv miss rates (Alex). Will post results in this thread.

Mike: I'll own the AB run, will tag results + raw traces.

Alex: thanks all — assigning to @Ben for the selector change and @Mike for AB. Will follow up with calibrator output later. :thumbsup:
